questions.prompt: In what order are the queues processed once the call stack is empty?

options.text: All microtasks in the queue are drained completely before the next macrotask is executed.
Only macrotasks execute; microtasks are dropped unless explicitly awaited.

questions.explanation: The event loop specification mandates draining the entire microtask queue before moving to rendering or the next macrotask.

questions.prompt: Why does the callback inside 'new Promise((resolve) => console.log('X'))' execute immediately?

options.text: Because Promise executor functions are called synchronously during object construction.
Because V8 compiles promises to WebAssembly.
Because it is hoisted to the top of the file.
Because console.log bypasses the event loop.

questions.explanation: The function passed to the Promise constructor is executed synchronously during initialization; only .then() and .catch() callbacks are deferred to microtasks.

questions.sectionTitle: Module 2: Asynchronous Event Loop & Concurrency Architecture Checkpoint
questions.prompt: How does Promise.allSettled differ from Promise.all?

options.text: Promise.allSettled rejects if any promise fails; Promise.all waits for all.
Promise.allSettled always waits for every promise to finish regardless of success or failure; Promise.all rejects immediately upon the first failure.
Promise.allSettled runs tasks in sequential order; Promise.all runs in parallel.
Promise.allSettled can only be used in Node.js.

questions.explanation: Promise.all fails fast on the first rejection, whereas Promise.allSettled waits for all promises to settle, capturing all results and errors.

questions.prompt: What happens if an error is thrown inside an async function without a try/catch block?

options.text: The function returns a Promise in the rejected state containing the thrown error.
The function converts the error to null.

questions.explanation: Any uncaught exception inside an async function automatically rejects the returned promise with the thrown exception.
